subtitle_zh: Matt Levine 与 Mary Childs 畅聊 Anthropic IPO 的 perp walk、CFTC 叫停 Trump 提及市场、以太坊三明治交易无罪案与假收购玩家。
summary_zh: 本期 Money Stuff 由 Matt Levine 与客串代班主持 Mary Childs 对谈，两人自嘲这是枚时间胶囊，因为 Anthropic 的 IPO 即将定价并交易。他们谈到 Anthropic 超额认购七倍、需求达 5000 亿美元，指出 IPO 需求常被夸大——投资者下大额订单笃定会被削减配额；Matt 解释 SEC 规定不重新申报扩募不得超过 20%。两人玩味 perp walk 一词，指 Hyperliquid 等离岸平台的股票永续合约在 IPO 前的走势，其 20% 溢价或许只是复刻 IPO 平均首日涨幅而无真正信息含量。随后聊到 Jensen Huang 绯闻、NVIDIA 创始地 Denny's 摘掉纪念牌，以及 CFTC 要求 Kalshi 下架 Trump 提及市场（尤其 Slopidopoulos 绰号赌盘）却保留其他提及市场。最后是以太坊三明治交易兄弟以诱饵订单反制抢跑者、被判不构成电信欺诈而无罪的案子，以及英国假收购定罪案；两人戏称假收购者只想角色扮演做大生意，还想开家叫 Fake Over 的酒吧俱乐部假装收购关键矿产和保险公司。

turns.zh: 播客。

turns.zh: 电台。

turns.zh: 新闻。

turns.en: You guys, did you see the massive geyser of rotting trash?
turns.zh: 各位，你们看到那个巨大的腐烂垃圾喷泉了吗？

turns.en: Oh yeah, it's at the end of Money Steps.
turns.zh: 哦对，就在 Money Stuff 的最后。

turns.en: That's so good.
turns.zh: 太棒了。

turns.en: Yeah, geyser of trash.
turns.zh: 是啊，垃圾喷泉。

turns.en: And did you see this skeet that was like, LA chose a new pope?
turns.zh: 还有你们看到那条帖子了吗，说 LA 选了个新教皇？

turns.en: That's really good.
turns.zh: 这个真绝。

turns.en: Hey Matt.
turns.zh: 嘿，Matt。

turns.en: Hello.
turns.zh: 你好。

turns.en: How are you?
turns.zh: 你还好吗？

turns.en: Welcome to the Money Steps podcast.
turns.zh: 欢迎来到 Money Stuff 播客。

turns.en: Right into it. We're the picture of efficiency today.
turns.zh: 直接开录。今天我们简直是高效的典范。

turns.en: I know. We're recording this at the worst time because this is going to come out on Friday and we're recording it at 2.30 on Wednesday.
turns.zh: 我知道。我们录的时间点最糟糕，因为这期周五才上线，而我们现在是周三下午两点半在录。

turns.en: And something's going to happen.
turns.zh: 而且肯定会出事。

turns.en: And so in the next like two hours, Anthropic is going to price its IPO. And then in the next like 22 hours, the IPO is going to start trading and events will occur.
turns.zh: 所以接下来大概两小时内，Anthropic 就要给它的 IPO（首次公开募股）定价了。然后再过大概 22 小时，这只 IPO 就要开始交易，届时会有各种事情发生。

turns.en: And all will be revealed.
turns.zh: 一切都会揭晓。

turns.en: We will not have talked about them. But you will get this podcast after they've occurred.
turns.zh: 这些事我们没法聊，但你听到这期播客时，它们已经发生了。

turns.en: This is a time capsule.
turns.zh: 这就是个时间胶囊。

turns.en: You'll be like, oh my gosh, I can't believe that Anthropic went to zero on its first day of trading. I can't wait to hear Matt and Mary discuss that. And then we'll be like, yeah, I don't know.
turns.zh: 你会想，天哪，真不敢相信 Anthropic 上市首日就归零了，我好想听听 Matt 和 Mary 怎么聊这个。然后我们会说，是啊，我也不知道。

turns.en: And they'll press play. And we're like, wow, a 20% pop. I expect a lot more. I think it's good.
turns.zh: 然后他们按下播放键，我们却说，哇，涨了 20%，我还以为会更多呢，我觉得挺好。

turns.en: I mean, I guess it'd be bad if it goes to zero, but it'd be kind of amazing if I called that.
turns.zh: 我是说，如果真归零那当然很糟，但如果被我言中了，那也挺神的。

turns.en: It'd be fun. Yeah. I love when a shocking thing happens so that you can actually observe your own mind processing something. Because when I saw the Jensen Huang headlines, the first moment I go, oh my God, something happened. Something actually happened.
turns.zh: 那会很有趣。是啊。我喜欢发生惊天大事的时候，因为那样你能真切观察自己的大脑在处理信息。我看到 Jensen Huang 那些头条时，第一反应就是，天哪，出事了，真的出事了。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好吧。

turns.en: Like I've been really bored or something. It's not true that I've been bored. So that's... But yeah, if Anthropic went to zero, something happened.
turns.zh: 好像我一直很无聊似的。其实我并不无聊。所以这……不过是啊，如果 Anthropic 归零了，那就是出大事了。

turns.en: Well, it's like every 10 years or something. This happened recently, I think, not in the US. An IPO will price... and then not actually trade, like between pricing and the actual distribution of the shares, they'll be like, something has gone horribly wrong and we have to pull the IPO even though we already priced it. It's like not really a thing that happens, but it has happened in the history of time. I don't think it'll happen to Anthropic, but like, man, that would be news.
turns.zh: 这种事大概每十年才有一回。最近就发生过一次，我记得不是在美国。一只 IPO 定了价……然后却没真正开始交易，就在定价和实际配售股份之间，他们会说，出了大问题，我们不得不撤回这只已经定好价的 IPO。这基本上不算常发生的事，但历史上确实出现过。我不觉得 Anthropic 会这样，但天哪，那绝对是大新闻。

turns.en: That would be so news. Wow. Would we do an emergency podcast? Should we decide right now? No, you won't do that.
turns.zh: 那可太是新闻了。哇。我们会做一期紧急播客吗？要不要现在就定下来？不，你不会做的。

turns.en: No, I will never do an emergency podcast.
turns.zh: 不，我永远不会做紧急播客。

turns.en: Really? Even if I call you?
turns.zh: 真的吗？就算我给你打电话也不行？

turns.en: As you taught me, there's no such thing as a podcast emergency. That's true. No, no, no.
turns.zh: 就像你教我的，根本不存在什么播客紧急事件。没错。不不不。

turns.en: There are no podcast emergencies, but there are emergency podcasts. You can't... Maybe there are emergency podcasts. The word order matters.
turns.zh: 没有播客紧急事件，但有紧急播客。你不能……也许真有紧急播客。词序很重要。

turns.en: Not the money stuff emergency podcast.
turns.zh: 但不会有 Money Stuff 紧急播客。

turns.en: Well, then we'll do an emergency stuff money.
turns.zh: 那我们就做一期紧急的 stuff money。

turns.en: That doesn't even make sense. Yeah, Anthropic, it's pricing today. It's seven times over subscribed. They're going to price above the range. They're thinking about upsizing it, the reporting is. $ 500 billion demand.
turns.zh: 这根本说不通。是啊，Anthropic 今天定价。超额认购七倍。他们会定在区间上限之上。据报道他们还在考虑扩大发行规模。需求高达 5000 亿美元。

turns.en: It's exciting.
turns.zh: 真令人兴奋。

turns.en: I don't know. I wrote on Wednesday... Everyone sort of knows that like IPO demand is inflated because people put in big orders and they actually want because they think they'll be cut back because there's a lot of demand. And it's like self-reinforcing. But like $ 500 billion is like, you know, if you want like $ 5 billion and you're putting in an order for $ 10 billion because you know you'll get cut back. Like what if you get filled? Like you don't have an extra $ 5 billion.
turns.zh: 我不知道。我周三写过……大家多少都知道，IPO 需求是被夸大的，因为人们会下大额订单，但其实并没想要那么多，他们觉得既然需求这么旺，自己会被削减配额。这就成了自我强化。但 5000 亿美元这个数字，你知道，如果你其实只想要 50 亿美元，却下了 100 亿美元的订单，因为你知道会被削减。可万一真给你全额成交了呢？你手头可没有多出来的 50 亿美元。

turns.en: It'd be so funny.
turns.zh: 那会非常好笑。

turns.en: It's all fun and games when it's a small IPO, but it's just a weird circumstance here.
turns.zh: 小规模 IPO 这么玩还行，但这里的情况就很奇怪了。

turns.en: They should just do it. Fill them all.
turns.zh: 他们就该这么干，全部满足。

turns.en: I know. Someone actually emailed me that.
turns.zh: 我知道。还真有人发邮件跟我这么说。

turns.en: What would happen? That would be so fun.
turns.zh: 那会发生什么？肯定很好玩。

turns.en: This is such a capital-intensive industry. If Anthropic just filled all $ 500 billion of IPO orders, it could use that money.
turns.zh: 这可是个极其烧钱的行业。如果 Anthropic 真把 5000 亿美元的 IPO 订单全部满足，这笔钱它用得着。

turns.en: They could use the money, okay? They need it. The economy needs it.
turns.zh: 他们能用上这笔钱，好吗？他们需要。整个经济都需要。

turns.en: You can't actually do that. I think there's SEC rules that you can't upsize an IPO by more than 20% without refiling. What? Why?
turns.zh: 你其实不能这么干。我记得 SEC（美国证券交易委员会）有规定，不重新申报的话，IPO 规模扩大不能超过 20%。什么？为什么？

turns.en: This is capitalism. Let them play.
turns.zh: 这可是资本主义，让他们玩呗。

turns.en: No, because the thing that you're marketing is not just... a company, it's also a capital structure. And if you're like, we're going to raise $ 60 billion, and then you raise $ 500 billion, you've misled your investors.
turns.zh: 不行，因为你营销的不只是……一家公司，还有一套资本结构。如果你说我们要融 600 亿美元，结果融了 5000 亿，那你就误导了投资者。

turns.en: Fundamentally changed the, yeah, fair. But at the same time, if you're capping it, the upsizability, then of course my order requests are fictional. I could say infinity. Just give me the max you'll give me.
turns.zh: 从根本上改变了，是啊，有道理。但话说回来，如果你给扩募上限设了封顶，那我的订单需求当然是虚构的。我干脆填无穷大好了。把你愿意给的最大额度给我就行。

turns.en: Well, but the actual risk when you put in a bigger order than you actually want is not that they'll upsize the deal too much. It's that they'll fill you Because nobody else wanted any stock, right? Yeah. Yeah.
turns.zh: 不过，你下了超过实际需求的订单，真正的风险并不是他们把发行规模扩得太大，而是他们会全额满足你——因为别人都不想要这股票，对吧？是啊。是啊。

turns.en: You're wrong about all your friends.
turns.zh: 你会发现你看错了你所有的朋友。

turns.en: Well, we were seven times over subscribed, but a lot of that, like they didn't actually want it. And so we're filling you a hundred percent. Like that's kind of bad.
turns.zh: 是啊，我们超额认购了七倍，但其中很多其实并不真想要。所以我们百分之百满足你。这就有点糟糕了。

turns.en: That's the bad version.
turns.zh: 那就是糟糕的版本。

turns.en: Yeah. Like one, you're getting more stock than you thought you wanted.
turns.zh: 对。第一，你拿到的股票比你以为想要的多。

turns.en: It could happen.
turns.zh: 真有可能。

turns.en: Two, like it's going to trade really ugly the next day.
turns.zh: 第二，第二天它会交易得非常难看。

turns.en: Yeah. No one else wants it. They already told the banker that.
turns.zh: 是啊。别人都不想要，他们早就跟投行说过了。

turns.en: Right. Like no one's going to buy it the next day. So you're, you're in trouble.
turns.zh: 对。第二天没人会买，所以你就，你就麻烦了。

turns.en: Yeah. Hope you really like it.
turns.zh: 是啊。希望你能是真喜欢它。

turns.en: But yeah, we'll see how it'll trade. You'll know by the time you listen to this. It's great.
turns.zh: 不过是啊，我们走着瞧它怎么交易。等你听到这期时你已经知道了。挺好的。

turns.en: And what about the perp walk? How's the perp walk going?
turns.zh: 那 perp walk（永续合约走势）呢？perp walk 怎么样了？

turns.en: Oh, you like the phrase perp walk for like.
turns.zh: 哦，你喜欢 perp walk 这个说法，用来指……

turns.en: I'm trying to formally establish this as vernacular.
turns.zh: 我正试图把它正式确立为一个通用说法。

turns.en: Yeah, it's actually a good one, right? Because like it's a specific thing, right? Like there's all these like offshore trading platforms that offer perpetual futures on stocks. But like there's a particular demand for perpetual futures. Like in the weeks leading up to the IPO, because they tell you where the gambling markets think the stock is going to trade when it opens. And right, like the trading price of the perps in the week leading up to the IPO could very easily be called the perp walk. There you go.
turns.zh: 是啊，这说法其实挺妙，对吧？因为它指的是一个具体的东西。有这么多离岸交易平台提供股票的永续期货（perpetual futures）。而在 IPO 之前的那几周，对永续期货的需求特别大，因为它们能告诉你，博彩市场认为这只股票开盘时会交易到什么价位。而 IPO 前一周这些永续合约的交易价格，完全可以叫作 perp walk。就这么定了。

turns.en: Let's do it. Let us know if there's a form that we need to fill out or someone we need to call, like a naming god. We can just make our appeal directly or everyone out there can just start saying it because it's cool.
turns.zh: 就这么办吧。如果有需要填的表格或者需要打电话找的人，比如什么命名之神，告诉我们一声。我们可以直接提出申请，或者大家干脆都开始这么叫，因为它很酷。

turns.en: Well, in any case, the perp walk is looking great. You know, the perps on Hyperliquid are trading at like a 20% premium to, you know, if the IPO price is like something like $ 80- ish, like above the, you know, they're marketed at a range of $ 70 to $ 78. So they're going to price above the range. If they price it like $ 82, the perps are like $ 97 or something. So it's like, it's kind of perfect. It's like a 20% pop, which is what everyone wants. But the thing is, like, the perps have a pretty good track record. It's not perfect. Not perfect. You know, the Bloomberg reporter was quibbling with like SpaceX's the perps overpriced where it would trade, where it would open.
turns.zh: 不管怎样，这个 perp walk 看起来很不错。你知道，Hyperliquid 上的永续合约交易价格比 IPO 价高出大约 20% 的溢价。如果 IPO 定价大概 80 美元左右——他们给出的营销区间是 70 到 78 美元，所以会定在区间之上。如果定在 82 美元，永续合约大概在 97 美元左右。所以这几乎完美，是 20% 的涨幅，正是大家想要的。但问题是，这些永续合约的历史记录相当不错，但并不完美。不完美。Bloomberg 的记者就曾挑剔说 SpaceX 的永续合约把它开盘的交易价位定得太高了。

turns.en: That kind of makes sense. And this could be that again.
turns.zh: 这倒也说得通。这次可能又是这种情况。

turns.en: Well, but also like, I don't know what the perps are pricing, right? Like what is the bet that you're making when you are buying the perps? Like one possibility is that you are, I don't know, you're like a market maker who is going to trade the stock the next day and you have reasons to believe based on like the man that you've seen, blah, blah, blah, that you think it'll trade at some price, right? But the other possibility is you're just like, look, IPO has popped 20%. Like that's the average, that's the normal IPO pop. So I'm going to buy perps at 20% above the predicted IPO price, which the IPO price is like $ 80- ish. We know that from what you've read in reporting about where the bankers think they're going to price the deal. And so if every perp just trades at a 20% premium to the IPO price, then on average, they will correctly predict IPO pops, but they will have no actual information content. And Anthropic could trade up 300% or down 50%. And the perps will be like, I don't know, we just bet 20%.
turns.zh: 不过，我也不知道这些永续合约到底在给什么定价，对吧？你买永续合约时下的到底是什么注？一种可能是，你是那种第二天要交易这只股票的做市商，基于你见过的种种迹象，你有理由相信它会交易到某个价位，对吧？但另一种可能是，你只是觉得，瞧，IPO 平均涨 20%，这就是正常的首日涨幅。所以我就在预期 IPO 价之上加 20% 买永续合约，而 IPO 价大概 80 美元左右——这个我们从报道里知道，投行打算把发行定在这个价。于是如果每只永续合约都只是比 IPO 价高 20% 交易，那平均而言，它们能正确预测 IPO 涨幅，但其实毫无信息含量。Anthropic 可能涨 300%，也可能跌 50%，而永续合约只会说，我不知道，我们就押了 20%。

turns.en: How old are these perp markets? Like how large of a sample set do we have?
turns.zh: 这些永续合约市场有多久了？我们的样本量到底有多大？

turns.en: Teeny, teeny, teeny, tiny. Like perp markets have been around in crypto forever, but like the pre-IPO, the non-hyperliquid pre-IPO perps, there's like, I don't know, there's like half a dozen examples and like half of them are Chinese companies and half of them are US companies. It's a small sample. It's like pretty good, but it's like a small sample.
turns.zh: 非常非常非常小。永续合约市场在加密圈已经存在很久了，但 IPO 前的、非 Hyperliquid 的 IPO 前永续合约，也就，我不知道，大概六个例子，其中一半是中国公司，一半是美国公司。样本很小。表现还算不错，但样本很小。

turns.en: So we're finding out every day how good they are. That's exciting. You, dear listener... Can tell us how good the, we don't know, we're in the past, but the listeners will know how good the perp walk was.
turns.zh: 所以我们每天都在验证它们到底有多准。这很令人兴奋。亲爱的听众……能告诉我们它有多准——我们不知道，我们活在过去，但听众会知道 perp walk 到底有多灵。

turns.en: It's true. It's true.
turns.zh: 确实。确实。

turns.en: Should we talk about Jensen again more?
turns.zh: 我们要不要再多聊聊 Jensen？

turns.en: I don't know. Should we? What's there to say?
turns.zh: 我不知道。要聊吗？还有什么可说的？

turns.en: I don't know, should we? Denny's took down the plaque.
turns.zh: 我不知道，要聊吗？Denny's 把那块纪念牌摘了。

turns.en: Yeah, like famously NVIDIA was founded by its co-founders sitting at a Denny's like sketching out on a napkin how they were going to start the company. And there's a plaque at that Denny's and they took down the plaque.
turns.zh: 是啊，众所周知，NVIDIA 是几位联合创始人坐在一家 Denny's 里、在餐巾纸上勾勒出创业蓝图创立的。那家 Denny's 原本有块纪念牌，结果他们把牌子摘了。

turns.en: So sad. That's the most damning thing.
turns.zh: 太可惜了。这是最能说明问题的一件事。

turns.en: Even if you've like downgraded your like personal heroization of Jensen Huang, like still, it's still cool that NVIDIA was founded at your Denny's.
turns.zh: 就算你已经下调了对 Jensen Huang 的个人英雄化崇拜，但 NVIDIA 是在你家 Denny's 创立的，这依然很酷。

turns.en: That Denny's. You gotta keep the plaque. You gotta keep the plaque.
turns.zh: 那家 Denny's，你得留着那块牌子，你得留着那块牌子。

turns.en: Maybe they're like adding a footnote to the plaque like now he is problematic. Yeah.
turns.zh: 也许他们是在给牌子加个脚注，说如今他有争议了。是啊。

turns.en: He did some gross stuff. I think that we just learned a lot about Denny's. And going forward, maybe we should start new companies in Waffle Houses. They're showing who they are, okay?
turns.zh: 他确实干了些恶心的事。我觉得我们只是更了解了 Denny's 而已。往后，也许我们该在 Waffle House 里创办新公司。他们暴露了真面目，好吗？

turns.en: I wonder where I'm going to start my new company. Probably not at a chain restaurant.
turns.zh: 我在想我要在哪儿创办我的新公司。大概不会在连锁餐厅。

turns.en: You don't have that many options in your town. Like that one coffee shop.
turns.zh: 你那个镇上没有多少选择，就那一家咖啡店。

turns.en: Probably do it in New York.
turns.zh: 大概会在 New York 办。

turns.en: You do it in the city. Yeah. No, that is so overdone. That's not a cute story at all. You're like, I was at the Carlyle.
turns.zh: 你在城里办啊。是啊。不，那太老套了，一点都不是个可爱的故事。你会说，我当时在 Carlyle 酒店。

turns.en: How many companies do you think even started at Balthazar?

And these brothers found this very crafty exploit where they could see that sandwich trades are going to happen. They could put in a lure order to get sandwiched. And then they had this trick to basically trick Ethereum into not doing the block that the sandwich traders thought was going to happen but instead doing the different block. And it's arguably a hack, right? It's arguably like it misused the code of this Ethereum block building thing incorrectly. But, you know, it's Ethereum. Code is law. Who's to say what is an incorrect use of the code? But so they did this a few times and they took $ 25 million from some sandwich traders and they got arrested and they got charged and they got prosecuted in the federal court in New York and They went to trial saying, no, we just used the Ethereum code the way it was meant to be used, and it worked. And he went to a jury, and the jury hung. The jury couldn't reach a verdict. And they gave the judge these sob stories. They were like, we were up all night. Half of us were reduced to tears. And so it was declared a mistrial.
